lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: What is the full form of MQTT?
back: Message Queue Telemetry Transport

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: Which standard body standardized MQTT in 2013?
back: OASIS

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: What communication model is MQTT based on?
back: Publish-subscribe model

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: What is a key characteristic of MQTT that makes it suitable for IoT?
back: It is a lightweight protocol.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: When was MQTT introduced and by which company?
back: 1999 by IBM

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: Name the three core concepts involved in MQTT.
back: Message broker, topic, and client subscription.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: What is the primary role of a message broker in MQTT?
back: Controls the publishing and subscription of messages, dispatching them between senders and receivers.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: For what kind of environments is MQTT designed?
back: Remote connections and limited bandwidth environments.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: What is a significant advantage of MQTT regarding its implementation?
back: It provides a very small code footprint.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: List the three principal components of MQTT.
back: Publishers (sensors), Subscribers (interested entities/applications), and Broker.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: Name the five methods associated with MQTT.
back: Connect, Disconnect, Subscribe, Unsubscribe, and Publish.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: How does the MQTT communication architecture differ from traditional HTTP?
back: MQTT uses a publish-subscribe (event-driven) architecture, while HTTP uses a request-response architecture.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: What does it mean for MQTT to be "event-driven"?
back: Data are pushed to clients whenever a specific event occurs.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: In MQTT, what is a "topic"?
back: A simple string that can have hierarchical levels, separated by a slash, used to categorize messages.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: Provide an example of an MQTT topic for temperature data in a living room.
back: house/living_room/temperature

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: What is the purpose of a wildcard in MQTT topics?
back: To allow clients to subscribe to multiple related topics without specifying each one individually.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: Which character represents a single-level wildcard in MQTT?
back: + (plus sign)

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: Which character represents a multi-level wildcard in MQTT?
back: # (hash sign)

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: If a client subscribes to house/+/temperature, what messages will it receive?
back: Messages for topics like house/living_room/temperature or house/kitchen/temperature, where + is replaced by any single arbitrary value.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: If a client subscribes to house/#, what messages will it receive?
back: All topics beginning with house/, covering all underlying hierarchical levels (e.g., house/living_room/temperature, house/kitchen/light).

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: Name two major cloud platforms that use MQTT as a primary protocol for IoT.
back: Amazon Web Services (AWS IoT) and Microsoft Azure IoT Hub.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: What is the secured version of MQTT called?
back: Secure MQTT (SMQTT)

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: What is the analogy used to describe the relationship between MQTT and SMQTT?
back: HTTP and HTTPS

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: How does SMQTT enhance MQTT?
back: By using different security features such as encryption.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: What is a key advantage of SMQTT's encryption feature, especially in IoT?
back: Broadcast encryption, where one message is encrypted and delivered to multiple nodes.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: List the four main stages of the SMQTT algorithm.
back: Setup, Encryption, Publish, and Decryption.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: What happens during the "Setup" phase of SMQTT?
back: Subscribers and publishers register themselves to the broker and obtain a master secret key based on the chosen key generation algorithm.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: What happens during the "Publish" phase of SMQTT?
back: The data is encrypted and published by the broker.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: What happens during the "Decryption" phase of SMQTT?
back: The encrypted data is decrypted at the subscriber end using the same master secret key.

lectureTitle: Lecture 6: Basics of IoT Networking-Part II
front: Are the key generation and encryption algorithms standardized in SMQTT?
back: No, they are not standardized; SMQTT is proposed only to enhance the security aspects of MQTT.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: What does CoAP stand for?
back: Constrained Application Protocol

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: What is the primary purpose of CoAP?
back: Web transfer in constrained networks with limited resources (energy, computation, bandwidth).

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: Which standard web protocol is CoAP considered an equivalent for in IoT?
back: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol)

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: At which layer(s) of the network stack does CoAP primarily operate?
back: Session layer, but can also be considered an application layer protocol.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: What type of communication model does CoAP use?
back: Request-response model (client-server interaction).

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: Which transport layer protocol does CoAP work on top of?
back: UDP (User Datagram Protocol)

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: Name the two main sub-layers of the CoAP architecture.
back: Messaging sub-layer and Request-response sub-layer.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: What is the primary responsibility of the CoAP Messaging sub-layer?
back: Reliability and avoidance of message duplication.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: List the four different messaging modes supported by CoAP.
back: Confirmable, Non-confirmable, Piggyback, and Separate.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: Describe a 'Confirmable' CoAP message.
back: A message is sent, and an acknowledgement (ACK) is received from the server.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: How does a 'Non-confirmable' CoAP message differ from a 'Confirmable' one?
back: For a Non-confirmable message, no acknowledgement is received from the server.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: Explain the 'Piggyback' CoAP message mode.
back: The server sends its response directly along with the acknowledgement message. Data is 'piggybacked' with the ACK.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: When is the 'Separate' CoAP message mode used?
back: When the server response comes in a message separate from the acknowledgement, potentially after a wait period. The client sends an ACK for the separate data.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: Name two HTTP-like functionalities supported by CoAP.
back: GET (retrieval), PUT (creation/repository), PUSH (update), DELETE (deletion).

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: Why is CoAP preferred over REST for constrained IoT environments?
back: REST is resource-hungry, while CoAP is a lightweight equivalent designed for low-power constraints and limited resources.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: What does XMPP stand for?
back: Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: What is XMPP primarily used for, and what is its underlying data format?
back: Real-time exchange of structured data, based on XML.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: How does XMPP's architecture differ from a traditional centralized server model?
back: It uses a decentralized client-server architecture, meaning no single central server is involved in message transfer.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: What advantage does XMPP offer in environments with firewalls, compared to protocols like PING?
back: XMPP can still work across networks with firewalls, overcoming obstacles that traditional PING might face.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: Name two key highlights or features of the XMPP protocol.
back: Decentralization, Open standard, Security features (authentication, encryption), Flexibility (interoperability).

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: What is the 'Jingle' core XMPP technology used for?
back: Multimedia signaling, including voice, video, and file transfer.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: Which XMPP technology is used for a publish-subscribe model?
back: PubSub (Publish-Subscribe)

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: What is the purpose of the 'BOSH' XMPP technology?
back: It is used for HTTP binding for XMPP.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: List one weakness of the XMPP protocol.
back: Does not support QoS, higher network overheads (not good for text-based communication), binary data must be encoded to Base64.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: Why is XMPP not ideal for text-based communication?
back: It involves higher network overheads.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: Name two applications that utilize XMPP.
back: Publish-subscribe systems, VoIP signaling, video/file transfer, gaming, IoT (smart grid), social networking.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: How does XMPP facilitate interoperability?
back: It offers flexibility in supporting interoperability between different systems, devices, and protocols.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: What is the main difference between XML and XMPP in terms of data handling?
back: XML is particularly used for unstructured data, while XMPP is useful for real-time exchange of structured data.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: Can XMPP communicate with other messaging platforms like ICQ or Yahoo?
back: Yes, XMPP allows communication with other messaging platforms in addition to other XMPP servers and intranets.

lectureTitle: Lecture 7: Basics of IoT Networking-Part- III
front: What is the role of the 'Core' XMPP technology?
back: It provides information about the core XMPP technologies for XML streaming.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: What does AMQP stand for?
back: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: Which ISO/IEC standard does AMQP follow?
back: ISO/IEC 19464

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: What is the primary purpose of AMQP?
back: To help define how messages are passed between business applications or organizations, connecting different systems and business processes.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: At which layer of the network model does AMQP operate?
back: Application layer (it is a binary application layer protocol).

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: What is the unit of data transfer in AMQP, and how does it relate to the link layer?
back: It is known as a 'frame,' but it is different from the frame concept in the link layer.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: Describe the basic operational model of AMQP.
back: Clients (producers) send messages to a server (broker), which then forwards them to other clients (consumers).

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: What role does the server play in the AMQP model?
back: The server acts as a broker, comprising routers, filters, and queues for buffering and forwarding messages.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: List four distinct entities that AMQP helps connect.
back: Organizations, Technologies, Time (different points of time), Space (different locations).

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: Name three key features supported by AMQP from a different perspective (beyond connectivity).
back: Security, Reliability, Interoperability.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: What does 'interoperability' mean in the context of AMQP?
back: Interoperability of not only devices but also protocols, algorithms, and messages.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: Explain the 'At most once' message delivery guarantee.
back: Each message is delivered at most once (once or never) to the intended recipient.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: Explain the 'At least once' message delivery guarantee.
back: Each message is certain to be delivered, but may do so multiple times.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: Explain the 'Exactly once' message delivery guarantee.
back: Messages will always certainly arrive and do so only once.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: What is the purpose of AMQP frame types?
back: To initiate, control, and tear down the transfer of messages between two peers.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: Which AMQP frame type is used for opening a connection?
back: Open frame type.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: Which AMQP frame type is used for closing a connection?
back: Close frame type.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: Which AMQP frame type is used for opening a session?
back: Begin frame type.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: Which AMQP frame type is used for closing a session?
back: End frame type.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: What is the function of the 'Attach' AMQP frame type?
back: Initiating a new link transfer for sending actual messages.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: What is the function of the 'Detach' AMQP frame type?
back: Terminating the link.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: Name the three primary components of the AMQP protocol.
back: Exchange, Queue, and Bindings.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: What is the role of an 'Exchange' in AMQP?
back: It is part of the broker, tasked to receive messages and route them to the queues.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: What is the role of a 'Queue' in AMQP?
back: Separate queues are used for different business processes, and consumers receive messages from them.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: What are 'Bindings' in AMQP?
back: Rules for distributing messages, determining who can access what message and their destinations.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: List the four different exchange types in AMQP.
back: Direct, Fan out, Topic, and Header.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: What does 'Persistence' imply in AMQP features?
back: Offering message delivery guarantees.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: Give two applications of AMQP related to system interaction.
back: Connecting different systems and processes to talk to one another; allowing servers to respond to immediate requests quickly and delegate time-consuming tasks.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: How does AMQP contribute to reliability and uptime of application deployments?
back: By increasing the reliability and uptime of application deployments.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: What is 'Targeted QoS' in AMQP?
back: It targets selective offering of Quality of Service to certain links.

lectureTitle: Lecture 8: Basics of IoT Networking- Part-IV
front: Name three AMQP frame types used for controlling message flow, state changes, or actual message transfer.
back: Transfer (for sending actual messages), Flow (controlling message flow rate), and Disposition (informing changes in state of transfer).

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What is the primary function of XMPP, MQTT, CoAP, and AMQP protocols?
back: Service offerings, operating at a higher level.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What layers are the focus of the protocols discussed in this lecture (e.g., 802.15.4, Zigbee)?
back: Physical and partially MAC (link layer).

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What is the primary use of the IEEE 802.15.4 standard?
back: Forming Wireless Personal Area Networks (WPANs).

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What are the typical data rate and power consumption characteristics of IEEE 802.15.4 networks?
back: Low data rate, low power consumption (extending lifetime).

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: Which two primary layers does the IEEE 802.15.4 standard focus on?
back: Physical layer and MAC layer.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: In which frequency band does IEEE 802.15.4 communication take place?
back: ISM band.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What modulation scheme is IEEE 802.15.4 based on?
back: DSSS (Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum) technique.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What is a key benefit of using DSSS in IEEE 802.15.4?
back: Highly tolerant of noise and interference, offers link reliability improvement.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What modulation schemes are used for the low-speed and high-speed versions of IEEE 802.15.4?
back: Low-speed uses BPSK; high-speed uses O-QPSK (Offset QPSK).

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What channel access method does IEEE 802.15.4 use for MAC communication?
back: CSMA/CA (Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance).

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: How does IEEE 802.15.4 minimize power consumption?
back: Infrequently occurring very short transmissions with low duty cycle (less than one percent).

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What is the minimum power level defined in the IEEE 802.15.4 standard?
back: Minus three dBm or 0.5 microwatts.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What is the typical transmission range for IEEE 802.15.4?
back: 10 meters to 75 meters (up to 1000m outdoors theoretically).

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What networking topologies are supported by IEEE 802.15.4?
back: Star topology and Mesh topology.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: Which variant of IEEE 802.15.4 is used for industrial applications?
back: The 'E' variant.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: Which variant of IEEE 802.15.4 is used for smart utility networks like smart grids?
back: The 'G' variant.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What are the two types of networks IEEE 802.15.4 can be classified into?
back: Beacon-enabled network and non-beacon-enabled network.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What are the two main types of devices in an IEEE 802.15.4 network?
back: FFD (Fully Functional Device) and RFD (Reduced Functional Device).

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: Give examples of Fully Functional Devices (FFD) in IEEE 802.15.4.
back: PAN coordinator, router, or device.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What are the characteristics of a Reduced Functional Device (RFD)?
back: Can only talk to an FFD, lower power consumption, uses minimal CPU and RAM.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: List the five frame types defined for IEEE 802.15.4.
back: Data frame, Acknowledgement frame, Command frame, MAC frame, and Beacon frame.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What is the purpose of beacon frames in IEEE 802.15.4?
back: PAN coordinator sends them to advertise its presence, enabling devices to know it's there and associate.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: How does Zigbee relate to IEEE 802.15.4?
back: Zigbee works on top of layers one and two of 802.15.4, extending functionalities to layer three and above.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What additional communication enhancements does Zigbee provide beyond 802.15.4?
back: Authentication, encryption for security, and data routing/forwarding capability for mesh networking.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What are the two primary components of Zigbee?
back: ZDO (Zigbee Device Object) and APS (Application Support Sublayer).

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What is the function of the Zigbee Device Object (ZDO)?
back: Device management, security provisioning policies.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What networking topologies does Zigbee support?
back: Star topology, Cluster tree topology, and Mesh topology.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What are the advantages of Zigbee mesh networks?
back: Fault tolerance, reliability, self-configuring, self-healing, extended network range.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What are the three main device roles in a Zigbee network?
back: Zigbee Coordinator (ZC), Zigbee Router, and End Device.

lectureTitle: Lecture 9: Connectivity Technologies- Part-I
front: What routing protocol does the Zigbee network layer use?
back: AODV (Ad hoc On-Demand Distance Vector routing protocol).

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What does "SixLoWPAN" stand for?
back: IPv6 over Low-Power Wireless Personal Area Networks.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What does the "Six" in SixLoWPAN refer to?
back: IPv6 (Internet Protocol version 6).

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: Which IEEE standard for radios does SixLoWPAN primarily utilize?

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: Why is IPv6 particularly suitable for IoT networks?
back: Due to its large address space, which is required for the vast number of IoT devices.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: How does SixLoWPAN enable IEEE 802.15.4 radios to access the internet?
back: Through header compression and address translation techniques.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What are the two types of addresses used for addressing in SixLoWPAN?
back: 16-bit short address and 64-bit extended address.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What is the purpose of the 16-bit short address in SixLoWPAN?
back: For PAN (Personal Area Network) specific communication, assigned by the PAN coordinator.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What is the purpose of the 64-bit extended address in SixLoWPAN?
back: For global unique addressing throughout the network.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: How are IPv6 multicast packets handled in SixLoWPAN, given that IEEE 802.15.4 does not support them?
back: They are carried as link layer broadcast frames.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: Name the three different types of headers in SixLoWPAN.
back: Dispatch header, Mesh Addressing header, and Fragmentation header.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What is the primary function of the Dispatch header in SixLoWPAN?
back: To identify the dispatch type (initiating/resetting communication) and the next header type.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: In the SixLoWPAN Mesh Addressing header, what do the 'V' and 'F' fields indicate?
back: 'V' indicates if the originator address is 64-bit (0) or 16-bit (1). 'F' indicates if the destination address is 64-bit (0) or 16-bit (1).

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What is the significance of the "hops left" field in the SixLoWPAN Mesh Addressing header?
back: It stores the number of hops remaining to the final destination node and is decremented by each node.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What is the key difference in structure between the first fragment header and subsequent fragment headers in SixLoWPAN?
back: Subsequent fragments include a "datagram offset" field, which is absent in the first fragment.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: Name the two routing protocols used in SixLoWPAN.
back: LOADng and RPL.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: From which existing ad hoc routing protocol is LOADng derived?
back: AODV (Ad hoc On-Demand Distance Vector).

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What are the three types of PDUs (Protocol Data Units) used by the LOADng routing protocol?
back: Load Request, Route Reply, and Route Error.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: In LOADng, who is permitted to respond to a route request?
back: Only the destination is permitted to respond; intermediate routers are explicitly prohibited.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What does RPL stand for in the context of SixLoWPAN routing?
back: Routing Protocol for Low-Power and Lossy Networks.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What routing principle is RPL based on?
back: Distance vector routing, adapted for lossy and low-power networks.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What are the two types of routing supported by RPL?
back: Proactive routing (for maintaining topology) and Reactive routing (for dissolving inconsistencies).

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: List some optimization objectives of the RPL protocol.
back: Minimizing energy, minimizing latency, and satisfying constraints related to node power and bandwidth.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What does RFID stand for?
back: Radio Frequency Identification.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What are the two main physical components of an RFID tag?
back: An integrated circuit and an antenna.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What are the two main types of RFID tags?
back: Passive tags and Active tags.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: How do passive RFID tags receive power and transmit information?
back: Through inductive coupling, where magnetic force fields from the reader induce current in the tag's antenna.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What is the key distinguishing feature of an active RFID tag compared to a passive tag?
back: Active tags have their own internal power supply.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: What was the predecessor technology to RFID, and what was its main difference?
back: AIDC (Automatic Identification and Data Capture); AIDC used wired communication, while RFID uses wireless (radio waves).

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: List three common applications of RFID technology.
back: Inventory management, asset tracking, personal tracking, access control, ID badging, supply chain management, counterfeit prevention.

lectureTitle: Lecture 10: Connectivity Technologies- Part-II
front: How is data stored within an RFID tag?
back: Data is digitally encoded in the integrated circuit (chip) embedded within the tag.
